items.summary: Recommendation: maintain financial containment, approve no discretionary spend or revenue forecasts, and preserve only already-queued reversible work after capacity release. Revenue is supported only for 2026-09-21: Amazon reports 6,219 clicks, 28 ordered items, 6 shipped items, and $4.92 commission, all in aggregate tracking ID "other"; named site rows show $0 site-attributed commission. Site revenue, contribution margin, ROI, and causal lift are therefore unknown. September AI usage is $1,002.46 across 5,531 calls and 39 instrumented sites, including 234 errors; AI cost per call is approximately $0.18, but cost-to-learn per proven outcome is not calculable because costs are not linked to measured outcomes. Infrastructure, hosting, domains, labor, and marketing spend are unavailable; fixed-cost, marketing-budget, revenue-target, and revenue-floor fields are blank. Do not claim profitability or extrapolate the one-day Amazon result to monthly revenue. Minimum finance evidence required for a valid margin view: period-aligned revenue by registered site/tracking ID, AI cost by site/task, hosting/infrastructure/domain billing, and any included labor or marketing costs.

Keep the 2026-09-21 Amazon result explicitly bounded: $4.92 aggregate commission cannot be assigned to a site, while named tracking rows currently support $0 site-attributed commission. Do not publish site revenue, ROI, margin, forecast, or causal-lift claims without period-aligned site identifiers and cost evidence.

Infrastructure spend is not calculable from the brief: operations has no deploy, uptime, error, or billing sweep results, and no fixed-cost or monthly spend limit is configured. Record this as an evidence gap in the finance baseline; do not access banking, change billing, or incur spend.
